answers.note: По рассказу Беды, Альбан укрыл у себя христианского священника, бежавшего от преследователей.
Томас Бекет, архиепископ Кентерберийский, был убит в 1170 году и причислен к лику святых в 1173-м.

groups.sourceReasons: RPO headnote states the pilgrims travel toward St Thomas’s Canterbury shrine; line 17 identifies Thomas Becket. This directly resolves the named literary destination.
groups.editorialReasons: Thomas Becket is the unique match to the named destination. The other English saint choices are plausible religion-history distractors; the RPO wording isolates the Canterbury-specific key. The easy calibration is borderline and recorded separately.

groups.sourceReasons: The same headnote says the Tales are a series of stories related by pilgrims on the way to the shrine; line 17 identifies Becket and gives 1170/1173.
groups.editorialReasons: The second sentence adds only that the journey frames the Tales, a direct paraphrase of the headnote. No cathedral-location assertion or other unsupported fact is introduced.

groups.sourceReasons: Bede I.VII says Alban “gave entertainment in his house to a certain clergyman, flying from the persecutors”.
